data.narrative:
Riverlane, a Series C-stage quantum computing company, is evaluated against a sector universe of 11 peers: 3 public companies (IonQ, Rigetti Computing, D-Wave Quantum) and 8 private entities including Quantinuum and Infleqtion.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation approach. Using Riverlane's $120M+ total capital raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C progression, this method yields $204M. A peer-median approach was inapplicable; while 6 same-sector peers exist, insufficient data points met narrow-filter criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier) to support robust comparable analysis—a minimum of 3 filtered datapoints was required.

The triangulated valuation range spans $173M (low) to $235M (high), centered at $204M median. This single-method result reflects constraint in the comparable universe; quantum computing remains a fragmented, early-stage landscape with limited public benchmarks and high heterogeneity in business model and technology maturity across private players. Key uncertainties include capital deployment efficiency relative to stage-typical burn, differentiation in error-correction approach versus leading competitors, and path to commercial deployment. Expansion of the peer dataset or introduction of revenue-based metrics would strengthen conviction in this range.
